passages.note: First-person campaign housing page backs state subsidies and bonds, zoning reform, and enforcing the Tenant Protection Act rent cap and local rent control (binding rules, which excludes rungs 4 and 5), but says nothing on building or running public housing, so rungs 1-3 are not separated.

Homelessness page commits to enforce the Tenant Protection Act's cap on excessive rent increases and preserve local rent control (a binding rule), but is silent on public housing; the rest is homelessness spending, which is adjacent.
Forum answers back a housing bond to finance affordable units, cutting red tape and local fees, and enforcing housing-element law; these show government action, but not which rung.
Debate answer: cut red tape, expand down-payment aid (demand-side), curb Wall Street buyers, and enforce the law that requires local governments to build; none of these separates the rungs.
Debate answer: expand down-payment assistance, limit Wall Street buyers, streamline CEQA rules; demand-side aid and deregulation do not separate the rungs.

Interview answer: trim regulations and fees, and fund the last tranche for about 40,000 shovel-ready affordable units; this is subsidy plus deregulation, with nothing on binding rules or public housing.
Debate answer: give builders an incentive by streamlining regulations and fees, expand down-payment aid, and fund shovel-ready projects; this shows direction only.
Forum covers biography, immigration, health care, AI and taxes; nothing on government's role in housing affordability.

rows.reasoning: His housing page pledges to enforce the Tenant Protection Act's limits on excessive rent increases and to "stand behind communities that have chosen to protect renters through local rent control". That is a binding rule on the private market, which excludes "Set no binding rules, but offer subsidies" and "Rely on the market". No passage addresses building public housing, so "Build no public housing, but set binding rules" cannot be separated from the public-housing rungs (silence is not a clause). The row shows a side, not a rung.
needs_source: Becerra's own words on whether the state should build or operate public or social housing (for example a candidate questionnaire answer on social housing or a state public-housing developer)

quotes.text: I will enforce those protections fully and stand behind communities that have chosen to protect renters through local rent control, within the statewide framework that keeps housing construction moving forward.
Everything will be on the table to close the funding gap – bond measures, state subsidies, public-private partnerships.
My administration will pursue zoning reform, expand by-right approvals near jobs and transit, and improve the laws allowing entry-level ownership options like duplexes and small condos.
I will also work with the Legislature to end the use of impossibly high affordable housing mandates as a backdoor to kill housing for families
